V2MIX -- verifier 2 (Method 2, torus covering, arb) generalized to per-cell radii h_r.   2026-10-01
Source: release_188_v3\upper_bound\verifier2\claimB_arb.py (v4), copied unchanged to claimB_arb_ORIG.py.txt here.
Independence: nothing from verifier1\, vpoly2.py or data\n1001\V1MIX\ was read or used.
Diff:  fc claimB_arb_ORIG.py.txt claimB_arb.py   (only the lines below changed)

CHANGES in claimB_arb.py
1. Config path.  CFG = os.environ['V2CFG'] instead of the release-relative ..\cfg_a42.json.  The env var is inherited
   by the spawned multiprocessing workers, so every worker imports the same file.  The banner now prints the cfg path,
   its sha256 and the set of distinct radii, so each log names its exact input.
2. Radii.  Old: assert str(d['h']) == '0.4952'; hq = F(619,1250) (one radius).
   New: hqs = [F(h)] * ncentres if "h" is a string, else [F(x) for x in "h"]; assert len(hqs) == ncentres and every
   h_i > 0.  Each h_i is an exact Fraction parsed from the decimal or p/q string (F('0.4952') == 619/1250 exactly).
   assert k == 24 and P1y == 0 kept.
3. Stage 1 (numba floats, UNTRUSTED).  stage1() takes the per-cell float array hr and h = max(hr).  The candidate disk
   for (cell i, translate j) gets radius hr[i] - j*delta - EPS_R (skipped if <= 0); the bin search window around a
   leaf center uses h = max h_i (any disk of radius <= max h containing the point has its center within max h).  Stage 1
   only proposes a certificate; a wrong proposal can only make stage 2 fail, never pass.
4. Stage 2 (python-flint arb, TRUSTED).  _ARB['h'] is now the list of exact Arb radii A(h_i); a leaf certified by code
   (i, j, a, b) is checked against the disk with center C_i + a P1 + b P2 - j u(tm) and radius h_i - j*delta, i.e.
   the radius of THAT disk's own cell i (i is read from the same code record that supplies the center and is asserted
   to be in range 0 <= i < ncentres, 0 <= j < NJ).  Everything else in stage 2 is unchanged: tree re-walked from the
   root grid (leaves tile [0, NX/4] x [0, NY/4] by construction), leaf squares rebuilt exactly from integers,
   TL, TM, TH, delta asserted exact, strict tests s = h_i - j*delta - rq > 0 and s^2 - |q - z|^2 > 0 certain in Arb.
5. Unchanged: check_direction_cover (exact dyadic/binary boxes tile [0, 3.1416] and 3.1416 > pi in Arb; every
   bisection's two children cover the parent, asserted tl < mid < th), the grid construction NX = ceil(L/(1/4)),
   NY = ceil(H/(1/4)) with the exact check F(NX,4) >= L, F(NY,4) >= H, exit status 1 on failure.

WHY IT STAYS RIGOROUS
 * Red contains each closed disk D(c_i + g, h_i), g in Gamma, for every i (the inscribed disk of cell i).
 * For theta in [tl, th] and delta >= |theta - tm|: |j u(theta) - j u(tm)| <= j delta, so
   D(c_i + g - j u(tm), h_i - j delta) is inside D(c_i + g - j u(theta), h_i) -- this is per disk and holds for any
   radius, so per-cell radii need no other change.  A leaf square inside the smaller disk is therefore inside
   Red - j u(theta) for every theta in the box, with the radius of the cell that named it.
 * Covering of the grid (hence of a fundamental domain [0,L) x [0,H) of Gamma = Z(L,0) + Z(P2x,H)) by these leaves
   for j = 0..NJ-1, and of [0, pi] by the boxes, is checked exactly as before.  So: no blue l_NJ.
 * Strict inequalities => also valid when cells are open.  Orientation of the 24-gons is irrelevant (only the
   inscribed disk is used).
 * The only global quantity that depended on h was the stage-1 bin window, which now uses max h_i; it is untrusted.

sweep.py: NOT generalized (heuristic / witness script).  Changed only to read V2CFG and to assert that every h equals
619/1250, so it cannot silently use the wrong radius on a mixed config.
